text: This is the do-this move.
Cairn sets a finish line he can see from the chair.
One session.
Not a new identity.
Not a rebrand.
When the spark dies, Cairn finishes the block he already started.
He does not hunt a cleaner calling on the same night.
He does not ask the room whether he is still passionate.
He asks what the next stone is.
Then he does that stone.
The question is small on purpose.
A small question can be answered with hands.
A soulmate question cannot.
The session ends when the block ends, not when the feeling ends.
Develop it is a verb he can do before bed.
Twenty minutes.
One paragraph.
One pass through the hard page.
The win is the ended block.
Not a restored crush.
Cairn can keep a promise to a pile.
Mood lies.
The pile does not.
If the spark comes back, good.
If it does not, the block still ended.
That is the only scoreboard tonight.
He does not need a law about every age group.
He does not need a wall of limits.
He needs a rule for this chair.
This week, when the side project gets dull or hard, treat that as the development process.
Not as evidence you found the wrong passion.
Finish the session anyway.
The grow group did not stay because the article got easier.
They stayed because their theory let them stay.
Cairn borrows that theory for one hour.
He can return the courtroom tomorrow.
Tonight he returns the chair.
He picks the next stone before he picks a new life.
He reads the next paragraph before he writes the breakup text.
He ends the block with the lid still open.
That is a session.
That is enough.
